findings.title: Reflecting request.referer as postMessage targetOrigin breaks resize and risks XSS
findings.body: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb line 11, request.referer (fully attacker-controlled header) is interpolated into a JS string as the second argument to parent.postMessage. postMessage requires an origin (scheme://host:port), not a full URL with path, so browsers throw and the resize message never delivers. It also reflects user input into script context; HTML-escaping does not make it safe inside <script>. Derive and validate the origin server-side from the allowlisted embeddable host instead of echoing Referer.

findings.title: Reversed postMessage origin check accepts wrong senders
findings.body: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js line 17, the check is `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) return`. This tests whether the configured discourseUrl string contains the message origin, instead of testing whether the message origin equals the expected Discourse origin. Any origin that happens to be a substring of discourseUrl passes, and legitimate origins with a path prefix can fail. An attacker iframe/window can then drive `iframe.height` resizing. Compare parsed origins for equality and validate height as a finite number.

findings.title: Bare open() on admin-configured feed URL allows SSRF and pipe execution
findings.body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 29, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open, not URI.open. If the value starts with `|` it can execute a local command, and http(s) URLs follow redirects, honor file-like wrappers, and have no timeout or size limit or error handling. A malicious or compromised feed URL can cause server-side request forgery, hang the scheduler, or execute commands. Use URI.parse + URI.open with explicit http/https allowlist, timeouts, size limits, and rescue network errors.

findings.title: Unrestricted open(url).read in import_remote allows SSRF via embed URL
findings.body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, import_remote does `open(url).read` on a caller-supplied embed_url with no timeout, size limit, scheme validation, redirect limit, or exception handling. TopicRetriever only checks the initial host equals embeddable_host, but open-uri follows cross-host redirects, so an attacker can make the server fetch internal metadata/cloud endpoints or large/slow resources and raise unhandled exceptions that fail the job. Restrict to http/https, disable/limit redirects, add timeouts, and handle failures.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes when feed item has no content
findings.body: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every RSS/Atom item has non-nil content. Real feeds often omit content/encoded body or provide only summary/title. Nil raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole hourly poll so no items are imported. Guard for nil/empty content and title/url before calling TopicEmbed.import.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx + expire throttle can leak a permanent throttle key
findings.body: In lib/topic_retriever.rb lines 27-28, throttling does `$redis.setnx(key,1)` then a separate `$redis.expire(key,60)`. If the process crashes between the two calls the key never expires and that embed_url is throttled forever (or until manual deletion). Concurrent processes can also interleave. Use a single atomic SET with NX+EX (setex/set with expire option) or Lua.

findings.title: Invalid X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL header
findings.body: In app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 28, the filter sets `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. ALLOWALL is not a defined directive (valid values are DENY, SAMEORIGIN, ALLOW-FROM). Browsers ignore the invalid value and fall back to default behavior, so embed framing remains unpredictable/blocked instead of explicitly allowed. Delete the header to allow framing instead of sending an invalid value.

findings.title: PostRevisor ignores validation/save failure and still reports success
findings.body: In lib/post_revisor.rb line 85, `revise!` was changed to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` but the return value is discarded and `revise!` unconditionally returns true, advances draft sequence, and triggers post-processing. When validations are enabled and save fails, callers (including TopicEmbed.import update path) believe the revision succeeded and still update content_sha1. Check the save result and return false/propagate errors on failure.

findings.title: Mutating caller contents string with << corrupts hash and causes duplicate footers
findings.body: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 13, `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller's string in place. If the same string object is reused, the footer is appended repeatedly, changing the SHA and triggering spurious revisions, and surprising callers that retain the string. Use non-mutating concatenation (contents = contents + footer or dup) before hashing/storing.
